title: To ML-Predict or Not to ML-Predict: The Impact of Machine Learning-Predicted Protein Structures on FEP Accuracy and Data Augmentation.
authors: Dryja, Parker; Muller, Morne; Horn, Monique; Balabin, Ilya; Dentmon, Zackery W; Rimal, Prawin; Peterson, Yuri K; Joubert, Fourie; Kaiser, Thomas M; Burger, Pieter B
journal: Journal of chemical information and modeling
one_liner_zh: 该文系统评估了ML预测蛋白结构（如AlphaFold2/3）作为FEP计算输入的性能，聚焦蛋白-配体复合物结构对自由能预测精度的影响，属于蛋白质结构计算与物理模拟结合的应用研究，但方法创新性有限。
abstract: The rapid advancement of machine learning (ML)-based protein structure prediction, exemplified by AlphaFold2 and extended by newer models such as AlphaFold3 and Boltz-2, has generated significant optimism for structure-guided drug discovery. In particular, ligand-protein cofolding approaches offer the potential to overcome limitations in generating starting structures for physics-based free energy perturbation (FEP) calculations. However, the practical readiness of ML-predicted structures for FEP applications remains insufficiently evaluated. Here, we systematically assess experimentally determined crystal structures, a homology model, and ML-predicted protein structures as inputs for FEP using a well-characterized congeneric series targeting the tyrosine kinase cSrc. A data set of 133 compounds was evaluated through more than 1400 FEP calculations under minimal optimization to approximate "out-of-the-box" performance. By maintaining consistent preparation protocols, we isolate the impact of structural origin on predictive accuracy. Variable performance was observed across both experimental and ML-predicted structures, highlighting that even under this idealized benchmark scenario, significant challenges remain in reliably generating and refining predictive protein-ligand complexes. This study demonstrates that predictive variation in micro and macro conformational states horizontal line rather than the structural source horizontal line governs predictive reliability, underscoring the need for careful validation when integrating ML-derived structures into FEP workflows.
abstract_zh: 基于机器学习（ML）的蛋白质结构预测的快速发展，以AlphaFold2为代表，并由AlphaFold3和Boltz-2等新模型进一步扩展，为结构引导的药物发现带来了巨大乐观前景。特别是，配体-蛋白质共折叠方法有望克服基于物理的自由能微扰（FEP）计算中起始结构生成的局限性。然而，ML预测结构在FEP应用中的实际准备程度仍未得到充分评估。在此，我们系统评估了实验确定的晶体结构、同源模型以及ML预测的蛋白质结构作为FEP输入，使用一个针对酪氨酸激酶cSrc的充分表征的同源系列化合物。在最小优化条件下，通过超过1400次FEP计算评估了133个化合物的数据集，以近似“开箱即用”的性能。通过保持一致的制备方案，我们隔离了结构来源对预测准确性的影响。在实验和ML预测结构中均观察到可变的性能，突显即使在理想化基准场景下，可靠生成和优化预测性蛋白质-配体复合物仍面临重大挑战。本研究表明，微宏观构象状态中的预测变异性（而非结构来源）主导了预测可靠性，强调在将ML衍生结构整合到FEP工作流中时需进行仔细验证。
